{{Quote|It is obvious these creatures are not covered by the Convention of Civilized Systems. The Jedi Council has no say in the matter.|Chairman Chi Cho, on the Talz|<ref name="Trespass" />}}
The '''Convention of Civilized Systems''' was a bill of rights that the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] ratified by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. It was put into effect to apply better methods of determining a [[Species/Legends|species]]' [[Sentience/Legends|sentience]], and it additionally granted the [[Rights of Sentience|rights]] of sentient Republic citizens to those who were deemed to deserve them. The decree provided various tests to ascertain sentience, and [[Arquata Station Amendments|amendments]] to the act expanded its coverage to species in multiple [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] that appeared incapable of [[Realspace/Legends|interstellar]] travel. However, the law in fact increased genocidal crimes against previously undocumented sentient species, as some individuals drove species to [[Death/Legends|extinction]] and then covered up the massacres so as to avoid prosecution by the Republic.

Besides these illicit [[speciecide]]s, another example of a failure of the law's enforcement occurred when [[Chairman/Legends|Chairman]] [[Chi Cho/Legends|Chi Cho]] of the [[Pantoran Assembly/Legends|Pantoran Assembly]] [[Battle of Orto Plutonia/Legends|declared war]] on the [[Talz/Legends|Talz]] tribe that had colonized the [[Water/Legends|ice]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Orto Plutonia/Legends|Orto Plutonia]], intent on discrediting their claim to Orto Plutonia and restoring that of the planet's [[Moon/Legends|moon]], [[Pantora/Legends|Pantora]]. The fiasco ended when [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Riyo Chuchi/Legends|Riyo Chuchi]] negotiated a peace agreement with the Talz, who were in fact sentient despite Cho's claims that they were not covered by the Convention of Civilized Systems.

==Description==
{{Quote|If the Jedi are able to communicate with them, their status is in doubt.|Senator Riyo Chuchi, on the Talz's level of sentience|<ref name="Trespass" />}}
[[File:Medcha_Wanto.png|thumb|left|250px|The Talz of Orto Plutonia were among the species whose sentience was questioned under the Convention of Civilized Systems.]]
The Convention of Civilized Systems was a bill of rights<ref name="Trespass Ep Guide">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode015.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Trespass}}</ref> that defined the methods of determining the [[Sentience/Legends|sentience]] of [[Species/Legends|species]] within [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] territory. The decree also afforded species the [[Rights of Sentience|rights]] granted to sentient Republic citizens if they were deemed to deserve them. The bill of rights offered tests to ascertain sentience, from tool use to evaluations of the species' complexity and its ability to "communicate advanced concepts" with members of other species. Under the law, standard protocol for first contact with an unfamiliar species was to transmit images of the species in question to Republic authorities to further determine the species' level of sentience. The [[Arquata Station Amendments]] to the bill of rights extended the decree's coverage to sentient species that lived in multiple [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] but appeared incapable of [[Realspace/Legends|interstellar]] travel, such as the [[Talz/Legends|Talz]] species, who inhabited both [[Alzoc III/Legends|Alzoc III]] and [[Orto Plutonia/Legends|Orto Plutonia]]. The Amendments' classification methods addressed everything from colonies that had "descended into barbarianism" to populations "seeded" by other species; examples of such species included the [[Arkanian/Legends|Arkanians]] and the [[Pre-Republic era|pre-Republic]] [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]].<ref name="OEG:S1" /> The Convention of Civilized Systems also held some significance in military matters, as exemplified when Republic [[Major/Legends|Major]] [[Kendal Ozzel/Legends|Kendal Ozzel]] took the decree into account when he was [[Battle of Khorm/Legends|captured]] by enemy forces on [[Khorm/Legends|Khorm]].<ref name="In Service of the Republic 1">[[The Clone Wars 7|''The Clone Wars'' 7]]</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|As an ''officer'' of the Grand Army of the Republic, I am not obliged to cooperate. Taking into account the ''Convention of Civilized Systems''—|Major Kendal Ozzel, to his captor, Asajj Ventress|<ref name="In Service of the Republic 1" />}}
The Convention of Civilized Systems had been ratified by the Republic<ref name="OEG:S1" /> and put into effect by<ref name="Trespass" /> [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the first [[Standard year/Legends|year]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="ERC" /> The law act's classification methods for sentient species in multiple systems were added and addressed by the Arquata Station Amendments to the original bill. However, unlawful responses to the law act occurred when several individuals went on to [[Death/Legends|exterminate]] previously undocumented and unidentified sentient species that were "found in inconvenient places," driving them to extinction before their level of sentience could be determined under the Convention of Civilized Systems. The killers then covered up the genocidal crimes to avoid detection and prosecution by the Republic. One such situation arose<ref name="OEG:S1" /> in 22 BBY,<ref name="ERC" /> when members of the Talz species was found to inhabit the [[Water/Legends|ice]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] Orto Plutonia, a presence that proved [[Pantoran/Legends|Pantoran]] [[Scout/Legends|scouts']] original reports of the planet's barrenness of life to be incorrect.<ref name="Trespass" /> Following the Talz's [[Skirmish on Orto Plutonia/Legends|attacks]] on the Republic's [[Glid Station/Legends|Glid Station]]<ref name="Trespass Ep Guide" /> and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]' [[XT Beetle Transport/Legends|base]] on the world<ref name="Trespass" /> as a response to the species' aggravation from the amount of military activity on the planet,<ref name="DB Talz">{{DB|species|talz|Talz}}</ref> an investigation team led by [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi Generals]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]—accompanied by [[Chairman/Legends|Chairman]] [[Chi Cho/Legends|Chi Cho]] and [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Riyo Chuchi/Legends|Riyo Chuchi]], dignitaries from Orto Plutonia's [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Pantora/Legends|Pantora]], which had previously laid legal claim to the icy planet—discovered the Talz on Orto Plutonia, who were led by [[Chief/Legends|Chieftain]] [[Thi-Sen/Legends|Thi-Sen]].<ref name="Trespass" />

[[File:Chi_Cho_insults_Thi-Sen.png|thumb|right|250px|Chairman Cho uses his interpreter, [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], to declare war on Talz Chieftain Thi-Sen before the Convention of Civilized Systems can take effect.]]
Unable to quietly exterminate the Talz—and thereby swiftly end the threat they posed to his leadership—because of the presence of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], who were the acting Republic representatives on the world, Cho instead [[Battle of Orto Plutonia/Legends|declared war]] on the Talz living there. In doing so, he intended to provoke a conflict that he hoped would leave the Talz colonists dead<ref name="OEG:S1" /> and therefore nullify their claim to Orto Plutonia and reinstate Pantora's control of the world. Cho himself claimed that the Talz were "little more than animals" and were not covered by the Convention of Civilized Systems, negating the involvement of Kenobi and Skywalker, who both objected to his aggressive course of action.<ref name="Trespass" /> However, Cho's assertions of the Talz's lack of sentience were not backed up by evidence,<ref name="OEG:S1" /> and he did not even allow the Talz to be tested for sentience in accordance with the Convention of Civilized Systems. Chuchi opposed Cho's claim that the Talz were non-sentient, but she was unable to prevent him from leading the dispatched forces of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] into war with the Talz. Cho was eventually killed, and Chuchi stepped in on behalf of the [[Pantoran Assembly/Legends|Pantoran Assembly]] to establish peace with the Orto Plutonian Talz, ending the short war and leaving Orto Plutonia in control of the Talz.<ref name="Trespass" />

Besides the bill of rights' role—or lack thereof—in the Orto Plutonia debacle,<ref name="Trespass" /> Republic Major Kendal Ozzel attempted to cite the Convention of Civilized Systems when he was captured by the [[Dark Acolyte/Legends|Dark Acolyte]] [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] during the Battle of Khorm in response to her interrogation attempts to glean information on the Republic's battle plan. However, Ozzel's claims did little to prevent the unfazed Ventress from intensifying her questioning by unhesitatingly killing several of Ozzel's fellow [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] hostages.<ref name="In Service of the Republic 1" />

==Controversy==
{{Quote|These creatures are little more than ''animals''. You can't ''lie'' to an animal. They can't be trusted.|Chairman Chi Cho, on the Convention of Civilized Systems' coverage of the Talz|<ref name="Trespass" />}}
Though not discovered by the Republic, a few conflicts stemmed from the bill of rights in regards to sentient species. Following the decree's ratification, some individuals executed [[Speciecide|genocides]] of entire sentient species before they could even be identified under the Convention of Civilized Systems, unlawfully violating and contradicting the law act's purpose to grant sentient species the common rights of Republic citizens. Although Chairman Cho wished to do this when the Orto Plutonian Talz were discovered, he was unable to do so with Republic representatives there to witness the crime.<ref name="OEG:S1" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The Pantoran Assembly's Chairman Cho thought Orto Plutonia's Talz were savages who didn't deserve the rights of sentient beings in Republic space—a claim Obi-Wan Kenobi knew wouldn't hold up under Republic law.|An excerpt from ''The Official Episode Guide: Season 1''|<ref name="OEG:S1" />}}
The Convention of Civilized Systems was first alluded to in "[[Trespass]]," an episode of the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' television series']] [[The Clone Wars: Season One|first season]], which aired in [[January]] [[2009]]. Besides receiving another passing mention in [[The Clone Wars 7|''In Service of the Republic, Part 1'']], the seventh [[Star Wars comic books|issue]] of [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (comic series)|''The Clone Wars'' comic series]], the bill of rights itself was not expanded upon in detail until the release of [[Jason Fry]]'s [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars – The Official Episode Guide: Season 1|''The Official Episode Guide: Season 1'']] in [[October]] 2009, which detailed the law act's structure and briefly recounted the role it would have played in "Trespass" had it been properly enforced.
